title: Practice: variables, formatted I/O & simple loops
overview: Four small judge-style tasks. They practise choosing the right data type, printing with a fixed number of decimals, reading a character after numbers, and using a `for` loop to repeat output or test each number from 1 to N.

concepts.term: Pick the type by the constraints
concepts.explain: Values up to 10^9 fit in `int`, up to 10^18 need `long long`, and fractions need `double`. Always read the constraints first.
`printf("%.2lf", 23.5675)` rounds to two decimals and prints `23.57`.
`scanf(" %c", &ch)` skips the newline left over from earlier reads. The other specifiers skip whitespace on their own.
`for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)` runs exactly N times. Start at 1 with `<=` when you need the numbers 1 to N themselves.
`i % 5 == 0` is true when `i` is a multiple of 5.

files.title: Add two big numbers
files.what: Reads two very large integers and prints their sum, using `long long` so neither the values nor the sum overflow.
files.output_note: 123456789012 + 987654321098 = `1111111110110`. That is far bigger than an `int` can hold.

check.q: Which specifier do you use to read and print a `long long`?

files.title: Read and print four different types
files.what: Reads an `int`, a `long long`, a `double` and a `char`, then prints each on its own line, with the double rounded to 2 decimals.
steps: Read `D` with `" %c"`. The space skips the newline left after the number.
Print them in order, using `%.2lf` for `C`.
files.input_note: Four lines: int, big integer, decimal number, character (this is the task's own sample).
files.output_note: Each value appears on its own line. `23.5675` becomes `23.57` because `%.2lf` rounds it.

check.q: What would `D` contain if you used `"%c"` without the space?
check.a: The newline character left over from reading `C`, not the letter `A`.

files.title: Print a line N times
files.what: Prints `I Love Practice` N times using a `for` loop.
steps: `for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)` repeats N times.
Each round prints the sentence and a newline.
files.output_note: Three identical lines, one for each loop round.

check.q: How many times does `for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)` run?

files.title: 1 to N with Yes/No for multiples of 5
files.what: For each number from 1 to N, prints the number followed by `Yes` if it is divisible by 5 and `No` otherwise.
steps: If `i % 5 == 0`, print `i Yes`. Otherwise print `i No`.
files.output_note: Only lines 5 and 10 say `Yes`, because they are the only multiples of 5 up to 12.

check.q: How would you change the program to say Yes for multiples of 3 or 5?

recap: Read the constraints first, then choose `int`, `long long` or `double`.
Use `%.2lf` to print a double with two decimals.
Use `" %c"` to read a character after numbers.
`i < N` starting at 0 runs N times; `i <= N` starting at 1 gives you the numbers 1 to N.

check_yourself.q: A value can be as large as -10^18. Which type do you choose?
Write a condition for 'i is divisible by both 2 and 7'.
